title: Recognizing the Unit Circle from a Parametric Plot
originalTopic: Identifying a parametric curve and its Cartesian equation
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Plot the parametric equations x = cos t, y = sin t for 0 <= t <= 2*pi. Identify the curve, write a Cartesian equation for it, and state the direction in which it is traced.
finalAnswer: x^2 + y^2 = 1 \quad (\text{unit circle, traced once counterclockwise from } (1, 0))

steps.title: Eliminate the parameter
steps.explanation: Squaring and adding the two coordinate equations removes t and leaves x^2 + y^2 = 1, the circle of radius 1 centered at the origin.
steps.why: The Pythagorean identity holds for every t, so every plotted point satisfies the same single equation.

steps.title: Track the starting point and direction
steps.explanation: The curve begins at (1, 0) and moves upward into the first quadrant, sweeping counterclockwise and returning to the start when t = 2*pi.
steps.why: Knowing orientation distinguishes a correct tracing from a mirror image and confirms the interval covers exactly one revolution.

steps.title: Set the display window
steps.mathExpression: [-2, 2] \times [-2, 2] \text{ with equal scale on both axes}
steps.explanation: A window of [-2, 2] by [-2, 2] with a 1:1 aspect ratio shows the full circle; a mismatched aspect makes it look like a tilted ellipse.
steps.why: Circle recognition depends on equal unit lengths on the two axes, which graphing software does not enforce by default.
